cycles.name: Groundwork
focuses: Rebuild knee-tendon capacity with isometric-led, carefully-gated loading.
Calibrate honest working weights on every lift and return to running on a 4-week ladder.

paragraphs: Groundwork is the cycle that buys everything after it. You're on court every day — the court already trains your speed and reactions; what it can't give you is a bulletproof knee and a strength base with real numbers on it. That's this month: tendon work that rebuilds the knee's capacity, honest baselines on every lift, and your first structured steps back to running.
The mental focus is patience at effort 6–7. Nothing this month is meant to feel heroic — it's meant to be repeatable, precise, and pass the morning knee check four weeks straight.
By August 24: working weights on the board, eighteen minutes of near-continuous running on a quiet knee, and a body ready for what comes next — where it gets heavy.
outcomes: Working weights calibrated on all five lifts
18 min of near-continuous running, knee quiet
Four straight weeks of passing morning knee checks
Iso holds built from 30s to 45s at real effort
The 5-touch week locked in around daily court time

cycles.name: Force Foundry
focuses: Heavy-slow-resistance lower-body strength — tendon remodeling and maximal-force foundation in one stimulus.
Walk-run becomes continuous easy running; deload closes the cycle.

paragraphs: Groundwork hands over your baselines — Force Foundry spends them.
Six weeks where the polite introductions end and the bar gets to know you. The same knee work that protected you this month becomes the engine of the whole program.
Every honest rep you log now decides exactly where the loading starts.
Heavy, slow, deliberate — earn the quiet knee, then we forge.

cycles.name: Hold Fast
focuses: Deliberate consolidation — strength held at maintenance while court and run fatigue is paid down.
First plyometric exposure as pure absorption: stick landings, step-downs, low pogos.

cycles.name: High Steel
focuses: Intensification on the primary lifts — fewer, heavier sets with full rest.
First jump production: single-response hops and snap-downs; strides return to the runs.

cycles.name: Spring Steel
focuses: Elastic conversion — repeated hops to bounds, lateral bounds last and fully gated.
Installs the permanent weekly template: the sustainable season standard.

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: Set the machine's range stop so your knees never bend past 90° — that's the ceiling this cycle. Start week 1 lighter than feels necessary; the first set's RPE tells you where to go.

Quads loading evenly, knees tracking over toes

exercises.note: Start light and treat this as pattern practice — a crisp hinge, no grinding. Next cycle loads this properly; this month earns it.

exercises.name: Machine Leg Extension

cards.title: Your Knee: The Ground Rules
cards.body:
After the 16k, your knee locked for two days. It's been quiet for a month — good — but quiet is something we verify, not assume. This cycle is built to load it carefully and prove it.

Normal and fine: muscle burn, effort, next-day stiffness that fades. Train through it.

Not fine: sharp pain, anything that radiates, numbness or tingling, pain that builds through a set — and above all, any catching, clicking or locking, or a knee that won't straighten fully.

  • Mild and fading → finish the set, note it in your log.
  • Building, or changing how you move → stop that exercise, use the fallback, message me.
  • Sharp / radiating / numb / any locking → stop the session, message me before the next one.

One more thing, on record: a physio baseline check now, while the knee is quiet, is the smart play. We train either way — but a locked knee that was never imaged deserves one professional look. Your call; my recommendation stands.

cards.title: The Morning Knee Check
cards.body:
The morning after any leg session or run, run this 30-second check:

  • No new swelling compared to the other knee
  • Knee straightens fully flat, same as the other side
  • Zero catching or clicking overnight or on stairs
  • Any soreness ≤2/10 and gone within the day

All four pass = green. That's what unlocks every progression this cycle — run ladder, box height, iso load. Any fail = we repeat last week's dose, no drama.

A fail on straightening or catching isn't a repeat — that's a message to me, same day.

cards.title: The Run Ladder
cards.body:
You're running again — on a ladder we climb together. Each week's rung only unlocks at our check-in, off a green morning check:

  • Week 1: 6 × (2 min run / 1.5 min walk)
  • Week 2: 5 × (3 min / 1.5 min)
  • Week 3: 4 × (4.5 min / 1.5 min)
  • Week 4: 3 × (6 min / 1.5 min)

Flat route, conversational pace — if you can't talk, you're too fast.

The ladder IS the run budget. No extra runs outside it this cycle — a spontaneous long run is exactly the move that cost you two days of a locked knee. Next cycle buys continuous running; this one buys the knee.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weights
cards.body:
The app never gives you a weight — you find it, the RPE target is the compass. RPE 6 means four clean reps left in the tank; RPE 7 means three.

  • New movement: start clearly lighter than you think. The first set's RPE tells you — too easy, nudge up next set; spot on, stay.
  • Week to week: hit the reps at or under the target RPE → small jump next time. At the ceiling, or reps missed → same weight again. That's progress too.
  • Rough day: readiness low, bar grinding harder than the number says it should → drop the weight. Regression is steering, not failure.

This month is calibration — every honest log builds the baseline the whole program stands on. Lighter and honest beats heavier and guessed, every single time.

cards.title: Period-Week Fallback
cards.body:
For the rough days, there's a pre-agreed fallback — so you never have to negotiate with yourself mid-cramp:

  • Full sets: the walks, all warm-up mobility, Glute Bridge work — easy movement genuinely helps.
  • Cut to ~2 lighter sets: Leg Press, Romanian Deadlift, Lat Pulldown, the Row — move the pattern, don't grind it.
  • Skip outright: Pallof Press, Dead Bug, Side Plank, Suitcase Carry — direct ab pressure waits a day or two.

Showing up for the fallback version counts as full adherence. It's in the plan because it is the plan.

cards.title: The Knee Heals At Night
cards.body:
Honest truth: 5–6 hours of sleep is the tightest limit in this whole program — tighter than any exercise choice. Tendon rebuilds on sleep; so does everything else we're asking your body to do while you coach and play daily.

Not asking for a life overhaul — aim for 7+ on the nights the week allows, and guard the ones before leg and run days first.

Sunday stays a genuine off day. No gym, no run, court only if you must coach. That's programmed, not optional.

cards.title: Your Week, Mapped
cards.body:
The default shape: Mon Lower · Tue Upper · Wed court only · Thu Walk-Run · Fri Control · Sat Easy Walk (optional) · Sun fully off.

Shuffle around your court schedule freely — two rules never bend:

  • Never put Friday's Control day right after the Lower day — the knee needs the honest 24h read between them.
  • The Walk-Run stays 48h+ after the Lower day.

Brutal week? Drop in this order: Saturday walk first, then the Control day. Lower, Upper and the Walk-Run are the core — protect those three and the week counts.

cards.title: Why Groundwork Looks Easy
cards.body:
You asked for 5+ gym days. You're getting three, capped at effort 7 — on purpose. You already train daily: every session on court is load. The gym's job is to add the one thing the court can't — maximal strength and a knee rebuilt to take it — not to compete with your sport for recovery.

So when a session feels like it ended with fuel in the tank: that's the design working. Don't add sets, don't add days, don't test the knee on the side.

This is a 24-week build and Groundwork is its foundation pour. Boring now is what brutal later is built on.
